summary: WizardConfigurator class is fully implemented at src/classes/Application/Admin/Wizard/WizardConfigurator.php in namespace Application\Admin\Wizard with declare(strict_types=1).

getRedirectURL() lazily calls createSession() on first invocation and appends ?wizard=<sessionID> (or &wizard=<sessionID> if base URL already contains a query string); subsequent calls return the cached result — fully idempotent.

createSession() calls BaseWizardMode::generateNewSessionID(), reads the newly created session data (which already contains sessionID/userID/lastActive from generateNewSessionID()), appends the InvalidationHandler with isInvalidated=false under key settingPrefix+'-invalidationHandler', writes step preselection values under keys settingPrefix+'-step_'+stepName, then persists via session->setValue().

comments.note: src/classes/Application/Admin/Wizard/WizardConfigurator.php: The use of AppFactory::createSession() in createSession() mirrors the same pattern in BaseWizardMode::generateNewSessionID(). The session object is re-fetched on each call. Since AppFactory::createSession() appears to return a shared singleton, this is safe; however, caching the session reference as a local variable (rather than calling AppFactory::createSession() twice — once inside generateNewSessionID() and once in createSession()) would make the dependency chain slightly more explicit if the session factory ever changed. Low risk given the current singleton pattern.

src/classes/Application/Admin/Wizard/WizardConfigurator.php: The class has no import for BaseWizardMode beyond the fact it is in the same namespace. summary: WizardConfigurator.php and WizardConfiguratorTest.php reviewed in full. Code is clean, well-documented, and architecturally sound. No blocking issues found.

Key format alignment verified: WizardConfigurator.createSession() constructs keys as settingPrefix+'-step_'+stepName and settingPrefix+'-invalidationHandler', which exactly match what Application_Traits_Admin_Wizard::getWizardSetting() produces (it inserts the '-' separator itself). The session contract between configurator and wizard is correct.

Read-modify-write pattern in createSession() is safe: generateNewSessionID() writes {sessionID, userID, lastActive} first, then createSession() reads that data and merges in the additional keys before persisting — preserving all initial keys. The wizard's initWizard() will find non-empty session data and will not re-initialise.
Idempotency is correctly achieved by caching $sessionID on first call and returning the cached URL on subsequent calls — no session duplication possible.
URL separator logic (? vs &) is correct and concise. QA confirmed both branches via edge-case tests.
All array literals use array() syntax as required by the project convention (AC #10).
declare(strict_types=1) present. No missing use statements — same-namespace classes require no import.

comments.note: WizardConfigurator.php line 84: getPreselection() returns the internal $preselection instance by reference. This is intentional (fluent builder pattern) and correctly documented. No action required.

WizardConfigurator.php: The class is appropriately small and single-purpose (SRP). Constructor injection of $wizardBaseURL and $settingPrefix is clean. The only external dependency (AppFactory::createSession()) is well-contained in createSession() and mirrors the pattern already established in the wizard trait itself.

WizardConfigurator.php: The two-call AppFactory::createSession() pattern (once inside generateNewSessionID() and once in createSession()) is technically redundant since both return the same singleton. However, this is a deliberate design echo of the existing wizard trait — it keeps the session access local to each method without introducing cross-method coupling. This is acceptable; a local $session variable cache would be marginally cleaner but not worth a rework.

Consider adding test_emptyPreselectionSession and test_redirectURLSeparator as companion tests with docblock explanations, or add a note in the existing class-level docblock listing these as 'verified via QA edge-case tests'.
